text: Temperature ≥ 38°C, headache, neck stiffness or purple/red rash, meningitis likely: give

detail.problem: All four parts encoded with the right concepts and threshold (Body temperature >= 38 °C, Headache, Stiff neck, Purpuric rash) in a probable Meningitis rule gated on Seizure, and the priority rule consumes it via (active_condition Meningitis). The page's comma list is read as 'any of', which is the literal reading of a 'Refer if any of' box; see rule-level note on how loose that makes 'probable meningitis'. 'Purple/red rash' is narrowed to Purpuric rash, which is the clinical intent (non-blanching rash) but drops a plain red rash.

Minor: meningitis rule additionally requires Seizure (page context implies it); priority relies on active_condition Meningitis, which may not match a system 'probable' diagnosis; 'red' rash mapped only to purpuric rash.

parts_missing: 'red' rash: only Purpuric rash is used. Petechiae of skin (disorder) is not a descendant of Purpuric rash, so a petechial or red non-blanching rash will not match
detail.problem: Every part is encoded: temp >= 38 °C, Headache, Stiff neck and Purpuric rash, OR-ed under Seizure, giving probable Meningitis, which the Urgent rule references via active_condition. But the OR reading means Seizure + plain Headache (very common after a fit) or Seizure + fever alone produces a PROBABLE meningitis diagnosis. As a referral trigger that is acceptable; as a 'probable' diagnosis it is over-broad and clinically doubtful. It also makes the separate new/worse-headache criteria redundant. Consider requiring >= 2 items (any2) or downgrading to possible.
